land.text: Cliopatria's Azerbaijan Democratic Republic of 1919 (72,209 km2)

predecessors.note: The Azerbaijan SSR "was established on 28 April 1920 after the surrender of the government of" the Democratic Republic.

successors.note: Renamed the Republic of Azerbaijan on 5 February 1991; independence declared 18 October 1991.

capitals.name: Baku
capitals.note: Infobox: Baku. It was a constituent republic of the Transcaucasian SFSR 1922-1936.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 83,457 km2 (the Natural Earth country, which includes Nakhchivan and Nagorno-Karabakh; the page gives no area): Soviet Azerbaijan in the borders it held from the Treaty of Kars (13 October 1921) to 1991. Cliopatria's Azerbaijan Democratic Republic is 87,458 km2 (1918) and 72,209 km2 (1919) and ends in 1919; the Soviet years lie inside its Republics of the Soviet Union and Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes. Nakhchivan came under the republic by the Treaty of Kars; the Azerbaijan page is silent on the Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast and Zangezur. [Reviewer eu-17-x: this keyframe now ends in 1921; from 12 March 1922 to 5 December 1936 the land is the Transcaucasian SFSR's (ledger loss and gain, and that dossier's keyframe); the same shape resumes in the 1937 keyframe.]

correction.text: Azerbaijan within Natural Earth borders, including Nakhchivan and Nagorno-Karabakh

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (reviewer eu-17-x split of the 1920 keyframe): the same shape from the dissolution of the Transcaucasian SFSR (5 December 1936) to 1991.

ledger.note: 1920, 28 April: "The Azerbaijan SSR was established on 28 April 1920 after the surrender of the government of the" Azerbaijan Democratic Republic.

1921, 13 October: the Treaty of Kars (Article V) "established the region of Nakhchivan as an autonomous territory under the protection of Azerbaijan", made up of the former Nakhichevan uezd, the Sharur section and southern parts of the Erivan uezd (Azerbaijan page: the "previously independent Nakhcivan SSR would also become an autonomous ASSR within Azerbaijan by the Treaty of Kars"). The TSFSR page dates a Nakhchivan autonomous republic to July 1920.

ledger.note: 1936, December: "In December 1936, the Transcaucasian Union was dismantled" and the Azerbaijan SSR becomes a union republic.
1991, 5 February: "Azerbaijan SSR was renamed the Republic of Azerbaijan" (sovereignty declared 23 September 1989).

ledger.note: 1991, 18 October: "Azerbaijan adopted its declaration of independence on 18 October 1991."

certainty.note: Nakhchivan's status before the Treaty of Kars and the Karabakh and Zangezur lines are not on the pages opened.
Kars border with Turkey and the Soviet-Persian line; internal Armenian and Georgian lines are the modern ones.

sources.title: Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 28 April 1920; Kars made Nakhchivan an autonomous republic within Azerbaijan; union of 12 March 1922; December 1936 dismantled; sovereignty 23 September 1989; renamed 5 February 1991; independence declared 18 October 1991; capital Baku; no area; silent on Nagorno-Karabakh and Zangezur.

sources.title: Treaty of Kars
sources.note: 13 October 1921: Article V places Nakhchivan under the protection of Azerbaijan.

sources.title: Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic
sources.note: Established 12 March 1922; dissolved 5 December 1936; Nakhchivan autonomous republic July 1920.

notes: No Cliopatria row after 1919 (Cliopatria's Azerbaijan Democratic Republic is 1918-1919; its Republic of Azerbaijan is 1992 on); the Soviet years lie inside Republics of the Soviet Union (1920-1921) and Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (1922-1991) shapes. The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union. Nakhchivan: the Nakhchivan SSR existed from 1920 (the Azerbaijan page calls it "previously independent"); it is drawn as a separate land only until the Treaty of Kars, and the counterpart string is not a slug because it lasted a year. Not on any page opened: the dates of the Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast and of Zangezur's transfer to Armenia, the Azerbaijan SSR area, the Sharur and Erivan parts of Nakhchivan (the Natural Earth region is the modern Nakhchivan, 5,311 km2). The Natural Earth Azerbaijan used here is 83,457 km2 against about 86,600 km2 in standard figures; the gazetteer undercounts it. Counterparts: azerbaijan-democratic-republic exists (Cliopatria); the TSFSR dossier is in this batch.
